title: Candidate segmentation and sensitivity
intro: A02 teaches interpretable, testable candidate segmentation. Synthetic browser exercises are linked to a native TIFF pipeline and quantified real-world failures on BBBC038/039.

scientific_context.caution: BBBC038 fixed bright Otsu+watershed official test object F1 0.385. Passing a synthetic challenge does not establish accurate nuclei or exopher identification.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → independent Prove → delayed review; then compare multiple real TIFF configurations locally.

goals.title: Background subtraction and binary mask
goals.why: Unsigned numeric overflow or unreviewed background subtraction can corrupt candidate masks.
explain: Background correction must be explicit and performed in sufficient precision.
A threshold selects foreground pixels, not whole biological objects.

worked_example.code:
import numpy as np
raw=np.array([2,250,20],dtype=np.uint8)
print(np.maximum(raw.astype(float)-15,0))
worked_example.predict: Predict the mask and candidate counts before running real Python.

goals.prediction_answer: Counts depend on threshold, polarity and the chosen morphological operation; they do not independently prove biological identity.
walkthrough: Name the intended object/background polarity before looking at the output.

Identify one failure case and explain how it affects a biological count.
investigate: Vary a threshold or minimum size; note when a candidate disappears.
Distinguish foreground pixel overlap from correct separated objects.
goals.debug_task: Explain one oversegmentation, merge or intensity-overflow failure.
goals.misconception: Every connected region is necessarily one correctly identified nucleus.
goals.scientific_boundary: Practice arrays and sample masks are synthetic. Real segmentation needs independent annotations and the same prespecified method on held-out images.

apply.starter_code:
# A02-G03 | APPLY | Filter small objects without silently merging
# TASK: Treat data.mask as binary 2-D; label 4-connected objects and keep only components with pixel area >= data.min_area; return result={'kept_objects':int,'kept_pixels':int}.
# INPUTS: data (see the lesson panel for values)
# OUTPUT: assign your answer to result

public_checks.assertions:
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
mask=np.asarray(data["mask"],bool)
labels,n=ndi.label(mask)
counts=np.bincount(labels.ravel())
valid=np.flatnonzero(counts[1:]>=data["min_area"])+1
kept=np.isin(labels,valid)&mask
result={"kept_objects":int(len(valid)),"kept_pixels":int(kept.sum())}
print(result)

public_checks.assertions:
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
from skimage.segmentation import watershed
mask=np.asarray(data["mask"],bool)
markers=np.zeros(mask.shape,dtype=np.int32)
for idx,(y,x) in enumerate(data["seeds"],1):
    markers[y,x]=idx
labels=watershed(-ndi.distance_transform_edt(mask),markers,mask=mask)
result={"objects":int(len(np.unique(labels[labels>0]))),"total_px":int(np.count_nonzero(labels))}
print(result)

raw=np.asarray(data["image"],dtype=float)
mask=raw>data["threshold"] if data["foreground"]=="bright" else raw<data["threshold"]
labels,n=ndi.label(mask)
areas=np.bincount(labels.ravel())[1:]
result={"candidate_count":int(np.count_nonzero(areas>=data["min_area"])),"areas_px":sorted([int(v) for v in areas if v>=data["min_area"]]),"validated":False}
print(result)

build_steps: Prespecify foreground polarity, threshold and minimum region size before processing.
Perform explicit source-preserving masking and connected-component labeling.
Remove only the objects specified by the documented QC rule; keep pixel-area units.
Test multiple changed input images and explain which biological claims remain unjustified.

review.title: Return later: independent segmentation transfer
review.why: Recall and transfer must be evaluated later without looking up the solution.
explain: An unfamiliar image tests whether the decision rule is understood.
Do not turn a practice check into an automatic research-validity label.

worked_example.code: print('A02 delayed review: return later and solve from memory.')
worked_example.predict: Predict the mask and candidate counts before running real Python.

review.prediction_answer: Counts depend on threshold, polarity and the chosen morphological operation; they do not independently prove biological identity.
walkthrough: Name the intended object/background polarity before looking at the output.
Run and inspect a changed threshold or touching-object input.
Identify one failure case and explain how it affects a biological count.
investigate: Vary a threshold or minimum size; note when a candidate disappears.
Distinguish foreground pixel overlap from correct separated objects.
review.debug_task: Explain one oversegmentation, merge or intensity-overflow failure.
review.misconception: Every connected region is necessarily one correctly identified nucleus.
review.scientific_boundary: Practice arrays and sample masks are synthetic. Real segmentation needs independent annotations and the same prespecified method on held-out images.

feedback.hardcoded: Compute from the image mask and parameters, never from one known answer.
